nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do income, urbanization, and natural resources affect the carbon footprint according to the outcomes of the study?
nodes.answer: The outcomes describe a positive role of income, urbanization, and natural resources in carbon footprint.
nodes.paragraph: The key challenges and best alternatives to environmental sustainability: a comprehensive study Syed Ale Raza Shah1 , Naila Abbas1, Luminita Serbanescu2, Rong Niu3 & Abdelmohsen A. Nassani4 In the modern world, the globe has been trapped by severe challenges, and an abrupt increase in environmental deterioration (ED) is one of these. The practitioners have recently tried to suggest several green initiatives to combat rising environmental concerns, but the problem remains intact. Most economies have priorities to meet their socio-economic target, and practitioners are unaware of true challenges and best alternatives. This study makes an effort to introduce the true challenges (income, urbanization, and natural resources) and best alternative (renewable energy, information & communication technology (ICT), and circular economy) for carbon footprint in the top 28 waste re- cycled economies (WRE) throughout 2000 2021. In order to obtain robust outcomes, the present study uses the most reliable estimators, and the Q-GMM is the most prominent. The outcomes describe a positive role of income, urbanization, and natural resources in carbon footprint.

nodes.question: In what way does LCA support business strategies?
nodes.answer: LCA supports business strategies by providing a holistic view of environmental footprints, which favors the full integration of circular principles into those strategies.
nodes.paragraph: 2019; Beylot et al. 2020; Schulz et al. 2020). As LCA is a standardised methodology, it guarantees rigour and uniformity in the calculations of environmental impacts, helping comparability of results and transparency in evaluation processes (Hellweg and Mil i Canals 2014). By delivering comprehensive quantitative insights, LCA supports the evaluation of alternative production pathways, fostering transitions from linear to circular systems and assessing the potential consequences of adopting alterna- tive productions (Prado et al. 2017; Br ndstr m and Saidani 2022; Sica et al. 2022). While a product may exhibit high circularity performance, this does not necessarily lead to a reduction in environmental impacts (Pe a et al. 2021; Roos Lindgreen et al. 2021). Therefore, LCA provides a scientific and methodological basis for measuring the environmental performance of products and processes within the circular economy, supporting more informed decision-making pro- cesses (Serenella et al. 2015; Byrne et al. 2017; Cordella et al. 2020). nodes.question: What is the focus of Fosten's (2019) analysis regarding CO2 emissions and economic activity?
nodes.answer: Fosten (2019) focuses on the short-to-medium run impact of economic activity on CO2 emissions, rather than the long-run Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC).
nodes.paragraph: There is a wide agreement about the link of CO 2emissions and economic activity; see, for example, Dong et al. ( 2017 ), among others. In general, models tting the EKC show very diverse evidence. Alternatively, Fosten ( 2019 ) focuses away from the long-run EKC and analyses the short-to-medium run impact of economic activity on CO 2emissions. In the context of the US, Fosten ( 2019 ) proposes a factor-augmented regression model to repre- sent short-to-medium run relationship between seasonally-adjusted monthly growth r a e so ft o t a IC O 2emissions and economic activity, which is represented by a single factor extracted using Principal Components (PC) from a set of macroeconomic vari-ables. He concludes that emissions are not linked to economic activity in the short-run (one month) but nds strong linkages when looking at cycles uncovered at time- scales of length one to three years.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Social|Decent work and economic growth|Sustainable enterprises|Carbon footprint reduction_qna_011
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the analysis conducted in the paper?
nodes.answer: The analysis focuses on the short-run relationship between economic activity and CO2 emissions in Spain.
nodes.paragraph: In this paper, we analyse the short-run relationship between economic activity and CO 2emissions in Spain, by tting a SADFM to annual rates of growth of Spanish CO 2 emissions with the factors extracted by 2SKF from a large set of Spanish macroeco-nomic variables. 2SKF is an unsupervised factor extraction procedure, which combinesinformation contained in all macroeconomic variables independently from the target variable. Additionally, we also consider factor extraction orientated towards pre- diction of the rate of growth of CO 2emissions. In particular, we extract factors using partial least squares (PLS) as proposed by Wold ( 1966 ). We conclude that the explana- tory power of selected economic variables is larger than that of common economic factors when the latter are extracted using the 2SKF procedure. However, the pre-dictive power of the common factors increases when they are extracted using PLS. We nd that the PLS common factors recover some explanatory power for explaining CO 2emissions beyond the information content of the selected individual economic indicators. Our results somehow differ from those found by Bennedsen et al. ( 2021 ) for the US economy as the outstanding predictors for CO 2emissions in Spain are private consumption and maritime transport of merchandise, while theirs rely more on IP .
